newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Tuntex plans US$3.2 bln LNG terminal.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Tuntex plans US$3.2 bln LNG terminal.

text.p: Taiwan's Tuntex said on Thursday it would invest US$3.2 billion to build a liquefied natural gas terminal and storage facility at Taoyuan in northern Taiwan.

The T$90 billion terminal, with capacity to import six million tonnes of LNG per year to fire a planned power station, would be Taiwan's first private LNG import facility, the result of an accelerating energy market liberalisation.
State approval must still be obtained to build and operate the terminal, a Tuntex spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
"We will build the project once we have government approval," he said.
The LNG facility would be build in northern Taoyuan county, home to one of the island's main crude ports operated by state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp.

To date, Chinese Petroleum is the only company allowed to import petroleum, including LNG. It already imports LNG through its southern terminal at Kaohsiung to supply gas-fired power plants operated by state-owned Taiwan Power Co.
Under a liberalisation approved in 1996, Taiwan's energy market is opening to competition, though the government has not yet made clear when or how LNG imports will be liberalised.

Tuntex, a diversified company with a focus on polyester fibre, construction and investment, has growing investments in overseas petrochemical projects -- and ambitions to enter Taiwan's long-closed energy market.
The Tuntex spokesman said LNG imported at its terminal would be sold to any gas-fired power station, including those run by Taipower as well as planned private power stations.

Ever Power IPP Co, controlled by Taiwan's Ever Fortune Industrial Corp, has obtained state loans and other financing to build a T$19 billion gas-fired power plant in Taoyuan to overcome chronic energy shortages at Taiwan's leading information technology industrial park at Hsinchu.
Details of how Tuntex would finance the LNG terminal were not available. The spokesman said financing would be worked out after state approvals are obtained.
Taiwan's first private petroleum imports are likely to be in the crude market, rather than LNG.
Giant Formosa Plastics group will begin importing crude to supply its new refinery and petrochemical complex once the first phase of the US$9 billion project opens in 1998 or even in late 1997.
